text:
Devon: After the 1.28 rolling upgrade in us-west-2, our GPU node pool ng-gpu-rtx stopped scaling up for pending GPU pods. Autoscaler logs are full of 'no matches for kind NodeGroup' and 'unsupported apiVersion' errors :confused:

maria: Which autoscaler are we running — upstream cluster-autoscaler or the forked one?

Devon: Deployed upstream manifests (kustomize) from infra repo. Image tag is v1.26.3. Logs attached below.

aj: paste the log snippet? suspect it is a compatibility thing with k8s 1.28 API changes.

Devon: ```
I0816 13:07:02.123456       1 node_group_utils.go:210] Error parsing NodeGroup: no matches for kind "NodeGroup" in version "node.k8s.io/v1alpha1"
I0816 13:07:02.123459       1 scale_up.go:345] Skipping scale-up: provider returned error: unsupported apiVersion for node group
```

aj: Yep — CA is trying to talk to a NodeGroup CRD that no longer exists under that group/version after the kube upgrade. Provider changed the CRD group for managed GPU pools during the control plane bump.

sre-oncall: Quick sanity: can someone run `kubectl get crd | grep -i nodegroup` and `kubectl get nodegroups -A` on the cluster? I want to confirm the new CRD name.

Devon: `kubectl get crd | grep -i nodegroup` -> `compute.gpu.redwood.io_nodegroups`
`kubectl get nodegroups -A` -> `No resources found in default` (because the kind name differs).

maria: So provider renamed the CRD from node.k8s.io/v1alpha1 NodeGroup -> compute.gpu.redwood.io/v1 NodeGroup. Old CA (v1.26) doesn't recognize it. Two immediate fixes: 1) update autoscaler to a version that has provider-specific CRD mappings for k8s 1.28, or 2) add a small compatibility shim that translates the new CRD into the shape CA expects.

aj: Option 1 is faster. Upstream CA releases after v1.27 include kube-1.28 compatibility. I tested v1.28.0-alpha locally and it recognizes custom groups. We should build/release a canary image and roll to one canary cluster first.

Devon: Spun up canary patch with image `gcr.io/redwood/cluster-autoscaler:v1.28.0-canary-2026-03-18`. Immediately after the rollout, CA logs show it discovered node groups and started scale-ups for pending GPU pods.

infra-bot: deploy: canary-autoscaler -> gcr.io/redwood/cluster-autoscaler:v1.28.0-canary-2026-03-18 deployed to cluster us-west-2-canary (by Devon)

maria: Awesome. Two follow-ups: 1) PR to bump image/tag in kustomize and add a versioned comment explaining this is a 1.28 compatibility bump. 2) Add a short e2e that simulates provider CRD renames so this doesn't blindside us next upgrade.

Devon: Opening PR now -> https://git.internal.redwood/infrastructure/infra/compare/update-autoscaler-1-28-bump-#3624

aj: Also add a transient alert: if autoscaler log contains 'no matches for kind NodeGroup' fire a P1 to infra-oncall for faster detection during upgrades.

sre-oncall: I've added a temporary log-based metric and alert in monitoring (rule id: MON-9812). Set to fire for 5 occurrences within 10m.

Devon: Marking this resolved for the affected clusters in us-west-2 and us-east-1 where we rolled the canary. Will schedule gradual rollout to remaining regions during low-traffic window tonight.

maria: Thanks all. Capture postmortem blurb in incidents channel after the global rollout. Note: cost impact minimal — some pending pods were queued ~8–12m before fix.

Devon: Follow-up: PR #3624 merged, rollout started, and I've added the e2e test in infra-e2e branch. Will tag owners for verification.

aj: Nice work. Adding to the 1.28 upgrade checklist: validate provider CRD group names and autoscaler compatibility.

Devon: Closing thread — will update incidents once all regions on new CA. :white_check_mark:
